ITEM.PTXT: All models adopt a double wishbone type suspension with trailing arms, in which the trailing arms and upper arms are made of steel plate, and the lower arms consist of a pressed steel lower arm No.2 and a lower arm No.1 with a toe adjustment mechanism.
The suspension geometry has been optimized, achieving excellent handling stability and ride comfort at a high level.
The instantaneous center (OR) of the suspension geometry has been brought closer to the height of the axle center. This suppresses squat during acceleration and lift during braking.

When driving force is generated at the rear wheels during acceleration, etc., the load on the front and rear wheels changes due to inertia. As a result, the load on the rear wheels increases and the rear of the vehicle squats. In anti-squat geometry, the geometric intersection point (OR) of the suspension is brought closer to the axle center; when the reaction force (T) of the driving force acting on the axle center tries to move the vehicle forward via the intersection point (OR), because there is an angle between the reaction force of the driving force and the direction of the intersection point, component forces are generated in the direction of the intersection point (T1) and in the direction of the ground contact surface (T2). By reducing this component force in the direction of the ground contact surface, squat at the rear of the vehicle during acceleration is suppressed.

Load transfer during braking reduces the load on the rear wheels, causing the rear of the vehicle to lift. In anti-lift geometry, the geometric intersection point (OR) of the suspension is set higher than the ground contact surface. As a result, when the braking force (BR) acting on the rear wheels is supported at the intersection point (OR), component forces are generated toward the intersection point (BR1) and acting on the ground contact surface (BR2). Because the force acting on the ground contact surface is in the opposite direction to the tire reaction force against the sprung load reduced by braking, lift at the rear of the vehicle can be suppressed.

The coil spring is separate from the shock absorber and is mounted lower, and a pigtail coil shape is used to reduce size and weight, accommodating the low floor package. In addition, spring insulators are provided at both the upper and lower ends of the spring, and their thickness is optimized to provide excellent vibration isolation and ride comfort.
The bound stopper is made of urethane to optimize the stopper characteristics.

Low-pressure gas (N2) sealed type shock absorbers are used to achieve stable damping force characteristics, achieving a high level of both steering stability and ride comfort. For details, refer to the shock absorber section of the front suspension.
The V-shaped design avoids the side members, achieving a low floor while ensuring wheel stroke.
Outer-tube bonded type bushings are used for mounting to the suspension member.
A ball bushing is used for mounting to the axle, ensuring high support rigidity.
A lower arm consisting of a combination of an arm with a toe adjustment mechanism (lower arm No.1) and a pressed steel plate arm (lower arm No.2), and a pressed steel plate trailing arm are used.
For mounting the lower arms to the axle, lower arm No.1 uses a ball joint and lower arm No.2 uses a ball bushing, ensuring high support rigidity.
An outer-tube bonded type bushing is used for the front bushing of the trailing arm, ensuring longitudinal compliance for excellent ride comfort.
A solid type is used. The stabilizer bar is mounted to lower arm No.2 via ball joint type stabilizer links.
Rubber bushings are used at the suspension member side mounting points.
A parallel cross frame made of hollow pipes and pressed steel plates is used.
High rigidity is provided at the mounting points of each suspension arm, ensuring excellent steering stability.
